finding.claim: Unauthenticated request body field `callback` is passed directly to axios.post, letting an unauthenticated caller make the server POST to arbitrary internal or external hosts. Redirects are followed by default, so a 307/308 can reach any internal host while keeping the POST method and body. The response leaks a success/error oracle per host and port.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), attacker-supplied JSON body on the unauthenticated pub router

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') route registered on unauthenticated pub router; no auth middleware in this file
req.body.callback read and passed as the URL argument to axios.post with no validation
res.json({status: r.status}) returns the status only for 2xx responses; errors and non-2xx throw, giving a success/error oracle

finding.guards_checked: No URL parsing, scheme restriction, hostname allowlist, IP/CIDR block, or maxRedirects=0 on this path. pub router has no auth middleware in this file. Mount point for pub is outside the repo; if it is only reachable behind internal auth, severity drops to MEDIUM. Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no auth middleware, URL validation, host allowlist, or maxRedirects=0. The only middleware is admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which applies to the admin router, not pub. No mount code in the repo applies auth to pub.
verdict.reason: The sink at routes.js:20 passes unvalidated req.body.callback to axios.post on the pub router, which has no auth in routes.js (admin.use at line 12 covers only the admin router), so an unauthenticated caller controls the URL; the trace at lines 19-21 matches the code. The mount point is not in the repo, so if it sits behind internal auth the severity drops as the candidate notes, but the verdict stands on the code available.

finding.claim: Admin-gated diagnostics endpoint passes the query parameter `url` directly to axios.get. An admin, or anyone holding an admin session, can make the server GET arbitrary internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), with redirects followed by default. Under the skill's rules, admin authentication does not close SSRF to metadata or RFC-1918 targets, so MEDIUM.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), attacker-controlled query string on the admin router

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies role gate to all admin routes
requireAdmin checks req.session.role === 'admin' and returns 403 otherwise
req.query.url passed to axios.get with no validation
res.json({status: r.status}) returns status only for 2xx responses

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin session role check only (routes.js:7-8). It does not validate the URL. No allowlist, scheme check, hostname/IP block, or maxRedirects=0. Admin role does not demonstrably imply OS-level access in this code, so it stays MEDIUM. Session creation and role assignment are outside the repo and were trusted as written.

verdict.guard_found: No URL validation exists at routes.js:15. The only check is the admin role gate: requireAdmin at routes.js:7-8, applied via admin.use at routes.js:12. That gate limits the source to admin sessions, so it is not a URL guard but it is the reason the source fails the low-privilege test.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:7-8, 12, 14-16), but the source is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker: `req.query.url` is only reachable after requireAdmin (routes.js:7-8, 12) admits an admin session, so the candidate's own admin-only premise fails the source check and the finding should not be reported as an unauthenticated or low-privilege SSRF.
